disclosures.title: Testnet only
disclosures.text: All Instaward work is built and validated on the Stellar test network for this sprint, and every Stellar Expert link on this page opens a testnet page. No real money moves on testnet. Orizon’s contracts are also deployed on Stellar mainnet outside this award; none of that deployment is funded by, or in scope for, this Instaward.

disclosures.title: Dispute credits are paid by the platform
disclosures.text: When a dispute is upheld, the partial-credit refund is paid to the buyer by the platform’s settler key, from the platform’s own account; it is not taken back from the agent’s operator. The platform, not an independent arbiter, decides whether a dispute is upheld: dispute resolution is a trusted, permissioned operation today, and the contracts have no on-chain refund function.
disclosures.changed_since_sow: SOW §3.8 says the refund is executed by the settler within the buyer’s authorization envelope. As built, the credit is paid from the platform’s own account instead of being drawn from the buyer’s authorization or from the agent.

disclosures.title: Agent endpoints are recorded off-chain
disclosures.text: An agent’s on-chain registration holds its owner, id, name, skills and price, and no endpoint. Which HTTPS endpoint Orizon calls for an agent is recorded by the platform, after the operator proves ownership with a wallet signature, and cannot be checked on Stellar. The SOW does not describe endpoint binding; it is stated here so nothing is implied.

disclosures.title: One platform key settles, rates and seals
disclosures.text: The settler, the role that executes charges and dispute credits, is a single platform-held backend key fixed when the contracts were deployed. It cannot be rotated, and there is no multi-signature or threshold control over it. On today’s testnet deployment the same key also holds the admin, scorer (reputation ratings) and sealer (attestations) roles. Settlement, rating submission and dispute resolution are therefore trusted, permissioned operations. Deliverable 1 makes registration permissionless; it does not make settlement permissionless.

notes.title: Testnet XLM, where the SOW says USDC
notes.text: The SOW words the settlement metric as USDC. On testnet, Orizon’s escrow settles in native testnet XLM. Where a settlement is counted here, it is labelled with the asset it really moved.

notes.title: The targets are SOW v4’s, not v3’s
notes.text: SOW v3 set lower adoption targets: at least 1 externally operated agent, 1 operator wallet and 2 settled workflows. SOW v4 raised them to at least 2, 2 and 3. This page measures against v4 only.

notes.title: Earlier self-payments are not counted
notes.text: The testnet escrow records charges from May and June 2026, before the sprint, in which the platform’s own wallet paid itself. No money moved between two parties, so none of them is counted as a settlement here.
